title: Project
text:
Card, D. and Krueger, A. B. (1994). Minimum wages and employment: A case study of the fast-food industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. American Economic Review, 84(4), 772–793.
On April 1, 1992, New Jersey raised its minimum wage from $4.25 to $5.05 per hour; Pennsylvania did not. The authors surveyed 410 fast-food restaurants in both states before and after the increase.

title: Project
text:
Take-home
The session covers one lab per block. Continue the project with the slides marked at home:

Replication package (Lab 3A): 00_master.R, README following the AEA template, Tables 3 and 4 (i)–(iii) within 0.01
The review: 2–4 pages, every citation verified, every number from output/
Slides: 5–8 slides (Lab 4A-b)
Your own configuration: keep CLAUDE.md, your skills and your verifier, and try them on your own project

Optional: send the review and the package to the instructors within two weeks for feedback.

title: Claude Code for Empirical Research
text:
Tuesday 15 December 2026, 13:00–17:00 · Room: TODO
Instructors: Tobias Hartl and Ines Wilms
A hands-on afternoon course on using AI coding agents, in particular Claude Code, in empirical research. You work in Claude Code inside VS Code from the first hour, on one project that runs through the whole afternoon and continues as a take-home.

title: Claude Code for Empirical Research
section: What you will be able to do
text:
What you will be able to do

Set up Claude Code in VS Code and choose a model, an effort level and a permission mode for a task, with plan mode as your default
Give a project a memory, rules, permissions, skills and hooks
Delegate work to agents with a specification and checks, and test the checks
Write a literature review and reproduce a published table with Claude, and verify every citation and number
Use AI in research responsibly: data protection, disclosure, specification search

title: Claude Code for Empirical Research
text:
The project
Card and Krueger (1994) studied the employment effect of New Jersey’s 1992 minimum-wage increase by comparing fast-food restaurants in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. In the afternoon you reproduce the paper’s main table, write a short review of the debate that followed, and present both in a few slides. Details and the take-home: Project.

title: Claude Code for Empirical Research
text:
Before the course
The setup is required before the course (about 30 minutes, no command line needed). Send the final check to the instructors; there is no time to install during the session. You need a paid Claude plan (Pro or higher) or a course account.

title: Claude Code for Empirical Research
text:
Data and AI use
Anything Claude reads is sent to an external server. Do not bring confidential data (CBS microdata, administrative registers, personal data, data under an NDA) to the course; we work with public data. Follow your doctoral regulations and the journals’ policies on disclosing AI use.

title: Setup before the course
text:
Required before the course (Tuesday 15 December 2026, 13:00). It takes about 30 minutes and needs no command line; there is no time to install during the session. If something fails, send the instructors a screenshot of the error before the course.


Go to claude.com/pricing, choose Pro (or higher) and create an account. The Free plan does not include Claude Code. If the course provides accounts, use the course login instead.



Claude plans


Optional: the Claude desktop app (claude.com/download) has a Code tab that runs Claude Code on a folder. It is a fallback if VS Code does not work on your laptop.



Download from code.visualstudio.com/download and install. macOS: drag Visual Studio Code into Applications. Windows: accept the defaults.



VS Code download page





Open the Marketplace page and click Install (allow the browser to open VS Code). Or, inside VS Code: click the Extensions icon in the left bar, search Claude Code, and click Install on Claude Code for VS Code by Anthropic (blue check mark).



Claude Code in the Marketplace


Install the R extension by REditorSupport the same way: open its Marketplace page and click Install, or search R in the Extensions view.



The R extension in the Marketplace





Install R 4.3 or later from cran.r-project.org. No extra packages are needed for the course project.
Install Quarto from quarto.org/docs/get-started (click the download for your system and run the installer), and the Quarto extension in VS Code (step 3). We use it in Block 4 to render the review and the slides.



Quarto download page






Make an empty folder, e.g. cc-test. In VS Code: File → Open Folder… (macOS: File → Open…), choose the folder, and click Yes, I trust the authors.



The trust dialog


Click the orange Claude icon at the top right of the editor, then Sign in, and finish the login in the browser.



The Claude Code panel in VS Code


Settings (Code → Settings → Settings on macOS, File → Preferences → Settings on Windows): search Claude Code initial permission mode and choose plan.




Type in the Claude panel:

Which versions of R and Quarto are installed? Do not install or change anything.

Approve the command Claude wants to run. Send its answer to the instructors by TODO date.



Do not bring confidential data to the course: no microdata under a data-use agreement (e.g. CBS remote-access data), no administrative registers, no personal data. Anything Claude reads is sent to an external server. We work with public data (Card and Krueger, 1994).




Not needed for the course. If you already use git, keep using it: commit before larger Claude tasks and review changes in VS Code’s Source Control view.



Claude Code also runs in a terminal. Not needed for the course.
# macOS, Linux, WSL
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
# Windows PowerShell
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

claude --version   # check
claude doctor      # check installation and settings
claude             # start in the current folder
